metadata.displayText:
Ok in the OrdersController.php there is a performance issue due to the code being setup without performance in mind. We are currently getting all orders when the endpoint is called resulting in 2001 queries being made and 7000 models retrieved. We are also looping the and creating an $result array instead of resource or DTO to map the object to be returned and a paginator so you are only retrieving a chunk of the data. 

As this would be an N+1 problem we should look to eager load here as well to reduce the number of queries required. When reviewing the the migrations i found there to also be a lack of indexes on the orders, orderitems, and customers tables.

As such we need to resolve this, my thinking is the following: 
1) Add missing indexes that would be of benefit to the orders index endpoint only (no scope creep here)
2) Update the OrdersController index method to use a resource and paginate on 50 results
3) Use eager loading in the index method of the OrdersController
4) Cache the response (we are NOT using redis right now so just put this as file based and lets have a resonable time before the cache is invalidated

In order to validate the issue is resolved before completing the above create a new unit test which will hit the endpoint and make sure there is no n+1 before the issue is fix this is expected to fail. After the above implemention the test should pass.

<?php

namespace Tests\Feature;

use App\Models\Customer;
use App\Models\Order;
use App\Models\OrderItem;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;
use Tests\TestCase;

class OrderPerformanceTest extends TestCase
{
    use RefreshDatabase;

    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        parent::setUp();
        Cache::store('file')->flush();
    }

    public function test_orders_endpoint_avoids_n_plus_one_queries(): void
    {
        $customers = Customer::factory(10)->create();

        foreach ($customers as $customer) {
            $order = Order::factory()->for($customer)->create();
            OrderItem::factory(2)->for($order)->create();
        }

        DB::flushQueryLog();
        DB::enableQueryLog();

        $response = $this->getJson('/api/orders');

        $queryCount = count(DB::getQueryLog());

        $response->assertOk();

        // 10 orders + 10 customers + 20 items must NOT produce ~21 queries.
        // Eager-loaded + paginated endpoint should stay flat (count + orders + customers + items).
        $this->assertLessThanOrEqual(
            6,
            $queryCount,
            "N+1 detected on GET /api/orders: {$queryCount} queries for 10 orders."
        );
    }

    public function test_orders_endpoint_paginates_to_50_per_page_with_resource_shape(): void
    {
        $customer = Customer::factory()->create();
        $orders = Order::factory(60)->for($customer)->create();
        foreach ($orders as $order) {
            OrderItem::factory(2)->for($order)->create();
        }

        $pageOne = $this->getJson('/api/orders');
        $pageOne->assertOk();
        $pageOne->assertJsonCount(50, 'data');
        $pageOne->assertJsonPath('meta.per_page', 50);
        $pageOne->assertJsonPath('meta.total', 60);
        $pageOne->assertJsonStructure([
            'data' => [
                '*' => [
                    'id',
                    'status',
                    'total',
                    'customer' => ['id', 'name', 'email'],
                    'items' => [
                        '*' => ['id', 'product_name', 'sku', 'quantity', 'unit_price'],
                    ],
                ],
            ],
            'meta' => ['current_page', 'per_page', 'total'],
        ]);

        $pageTwo = $this->getJson('/api/orders?page=2');
        $pageTwo->assertOk();
        $pageTwo->assertJsonCount(10, 'data');
        $pageTwo->assertJsonPath('meta.current_page', 2);
    }

    public function test_orders_endpoint_caches_response_using_file_store(): void
    {
        $customer = Customer::factory()->create();
        $order = Order::factory()->for($customer)->create();
        OrderItem::factory(2)->for($order)->create();

        $first = $this->getJson('/api/orders');
        $first->assertOk();

        $this->assertTrue(
            Cache::store('file')->has('orders:index:page:1'),
            'Expected orders index response to be cached in the file store.'
        );

        DB::flushQueryLog();
        DB::enableQueryLog();

        $second = $this->getJson('/api/orders');
        $second->assertOk();

        $this->assertEquals($first->json(), $second->json(), 'Cached response should match the original response.');
        $this->assertCount(0, DB::getQueryLog(), 'Cached response should not hit the database.');
    }

    public function test_supporting_indexes_exist_for_orders_index_endpoint(): void
    {
        $orderIndexes = collect(Schema::getIndexes('orders'))->pluck('columns')->map(
            fn ($columns) => (array) $columns
        );
        $itemIndexes = collect(Schema::getIndexes('order_items'))->pluck('columns')->map(
            fn ($columns) => (array) $columns
        );

        $this->assertTrue(
            $orderIndexes->contains(fn ($columns) => $columns === ['customer_id']),
            'Missing index on orders.customer_id (customer eager load / FK join).'
        );
        $this->assertTrue(
            $orderIndexes->contains(fn ($columns) => $columns === ['created_at']),
            'Missing index on orders.created_at (latest() pagination ordering).'
        );
        $this->assertTrue(
            $itemIndexes->contains(fn ($columns) => $columns === ['order_id']),
            'Missing index on order_items.order_id (items eager load).'
        );
    }
}

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Http\Resources\OrderResource;
use App\Models\Order;
use Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;

class OrderController extends Controller
{
    public function index(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        $page = $request->integer('page', 1);
        $cacheKey = "orders:index:page:{$page}";

        // Plain arrays are cached (not the paginator itself) because the app
        // disallows unserializing PHP classes from cache
        // (`cache.serializable_classes` is false).
        $data = Cache::store('file')->remember($cacheKey, now()->addMinutes(10), function () {
            $orders = Order::with(['customer', 'items'])->latest()->paginate(50);

            return OrderResource::collection($orders)->response()->getData(true);
        });

        return response()->json($data);
    }
}

Fixed, and the "1 order" symptom had a concrete root cause — it wasn't the query logic.

**Why you saw 1 order:** a stale *test* response was sitting in the shared file cache. I dumped it: one order ("Jane Doe", from `test_order_includes_correct_customer`), `meta.total: 1`, valid until 17:43. The tests flush the file cache in `setUp` but left populated entries behind, and since the endpoint uses that same file store, your dev database hits kept serving the cached test payload instead of the real 1000 orders. I cleared it, and closed the hole three ways:
- cache keys are now env-scoped (`orders:index:{env}:page:{n}`), so `testing` and `local` traffic can never share entries;
- both test files flush the file store in `tearDown` as well as `setUp` — verified the cache dir is empty after a full run;
- result holds: re-hit the endpoint now and you should get 50/page across 20 pages.

**`latest()` removed** — fair point, you didn't ask for it. The controller is now exactly what you specified: `Order::with(['customer', 'items'])->paginate(50)` + resource + file cache (10 min). As a consequence I also removed the `orders.created_at` index from the migration, since its only justification was the `latest()` ordering. Remaining indexes: `orders.customer_id`, `order_items.order_id`.

One action on your side: if the earlier migration already ran against your dev MySQL, the `created_at` index still exists there (editing the file doesn't retract it). Drop it with:
```sql
DROP INDEX orders_created_at_index ON orders;
```
Not needed in test/CI — `RefreshDatabase` rebuilds from the current file.

Full suite: **23/23 passing**.

        return OrderResource::collection($orders);
    }
}
